sentences.text: The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1623/2014 on the file of the Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode is the appellant herein.

sentences.text: (For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Sections 140 and 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 17.6.2014.

According to the petitioner, on 17.6.2014. at about 10.30 a.m., while he was riding a motor cycle, a jeep bearing registration No.KL 09-E-1031 owned by the 1st respondent and negligently driven by the 2 nd respondent knocked him down and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2 nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver 2025:KER:31547 of the offending vehicle.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A9 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,32,896/- rounded to Rs.4,32,900/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. V.N. Ramesan Nambisan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant,
and Sri. Aginov Mathappan, the 2025:KER:31547 learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.

2 10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as a Headmaster in a UP School, getting a monthly income of Rs.45,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income of more than Rs.10,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
11. From Ext.A6 salary certificate, it is proved that the petitioner was working as Headmaster and getting a monthly salary of Rs.43,984/-.

Since because of the injuries sustained in the accident, he has not lost his job and there was no reduction in the salary, for the purpose of assessing the loss of disability, his notional income is fixed at 50% of the salary, which will come to Rs.22,000/-
(approximately).

12. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"1. Open fracture both bone right leg (Tibia & Fibula)
2. Pain, deformity and wound right leg.
3. Conscious oriented with stable vitals.

4. Laceration 3x1 cm over right Shin.
5.
Laceration 2x1 cm just above ankle.

6. Abrasions of 10x5 cm over right shin.
7.
Wound debridement 8.
Non-Union fracture tibia requires intramedullary nailing.

9. Non-Union, compartment syndrome, future bone grafting.
10. Re-debridement and IM nailing right tibia done."

13. As per Exhibit C1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, the petitioner suffered 18%
permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and hence, I do not find any grounds to interfere with the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 18%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 53 years.

Therefore, 15% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to 2025:KER:31547 Rs.6,01,128/-.
15.
According to the learned counsel, the petitioner has availed leave for a period of 73 days, because of the injuries sustained in the accident.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.1,02,028/-.
Since his monthly salary is Rs.43,984/- the salary for a period of 73 days will come to Rs.1,07,027/-(43984/3073).
Therefore, towards 'loss of earning' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.1,07,027/-.
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.10,000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
Towards 'extra nourishment' nothing was awarded.
17. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 7 days.

Because of the injuries sustained and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and 2025:KER:31547 sufferings'
and 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.75,000/-, and 50,000/- respectively.
Towards the head 'extra nourishment' the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.5,000/-.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.9,44,623/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

sentences.text:
In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.9,44,623/- (Rupees nine lakh forty four thousand six hundred and twenty three only),
less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal,
from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 253 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).
21.
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
